humanities_role_explanation: Evaluates LLMs on their domain-specific philological competence in diplomatic transcription, requiring preservation of 18th-century orthography and using specialized metrics like HCPR and AIR to detect temporal/historical language biases.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Multimodal evaluation where models receive page images of scanned books along with textual transcription prompts, outputting structured textual transcriptions.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Diplomatic transcription of historical 18th-century Russian Civil font, visual recognition of obsolete/period-specific Cyrillic characters from page scans, and post-OCR textual correction.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: The evaluation framework and dataset are highly specialized and scoped to historical document OCR, specifically 18th-century Russian Civil font texts.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates 12 leading LLMs including Claude 3.5/3.7, GPT-4o/4.1, Gemini 2.0/2.5, Qwen-2.5-VL, and Llama-4.

quantitative_metrics.note: Uses standard OCR metrics (CER, WER, CaseER) alongside newly proposed domain-specific metrics (HCPR, AIR) and statistical stability measures (CV).

published_after_march_2023.note: Published in September 2025 at the RANLP Workshop on NLP and Language Models for Digital Humanities.

summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework for LLM-based historical document OCR, utilizing a novel dataset of 18th-century Russian Civil font prints. To address the limitations of standard metrics, the author introduces domain-specific metrics (HCPR and AIR) to evaluate historical orthographic accuracy and reveal temporal biases in generative models.
key_findings: Gemini 2.5 Pro and Qwen 2.5-VL emerged as the most stable and accurate models, substantially outperforming traditional OCR tools. However, the study identifies a systematic 'over-historicization' bias where models incorrectly insert pre-Petrine archaic characters (e.g., big/little yus, omega) that were already obsolete. Furthermore, post-OCR text correction actually degraded transcription quality compared to direct image-based OCR.
facets_explanation: The ground truth transcription was created by a single expert annotator who performed a 100% manual review and correction of the corpus using eScriptorium to ensure diplomatic fidelity. A second verifier audited a sample of 500 lines, showing high agreement (98.6% line-level exact-match), which was used to validate the dataset accuracy rather than to preserve interpretive divergence. The models are evaluated using character and word error rates against this single, definitive reference transcription.
results_explanation: The best-performing model, Gemini-2.5-Pro, achieved a headline Character Error Rate of 3.36% ('cer') in full page mode (Table 3). A human verification audit of 500 lines reported that 'character-level accuracy was 99.93%', which compared to Gemini's 96.64% character accuracy (derived as 100 - 3.36% CER) yields a human-model gap of 3.29 percentage points (rounded to 3). The largest format/processing gap occurs for Gemini-2.5-Flash, whose WER degrades from '6.70%' in Full page mode to '30.77%' in Sliding Window mode (Table 2), a gap of 24.07 percentage points (rounded to 24).
